text:
nisha: Heads up — after the 6.4 kernel roll in eu-west2 the p4 fleet is hitting module load failures on boot. modprobe fails with 'Module nvidia not found in /lib/modules/6.4.0-rc...'.
chris: Confirmed on ~30 nodes. Jobs see NCCL handshake timeouts and long stalls. GPU sessions drop during init.
nisha: DKMS build step seems to fail during our node-init: 'ERROR: Cannot find the kernel headers for 6.4.0-rc' and then depmod skips nvidia.
chris: I grabbed a node console, there's also a symbol version mismatch: 'nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout' in dmesg. That smells like driver <-> kernel ABI mismatch, not just missing headers.
eng-sre-bot: deploybot: rollback policy triggered for kernel-rollout/eu-west2 at 12:05 UTC — pausing further kernel upgrades. Incident INC-2028-451 opened in #incidents.
leo: Mitigation plan: pause auto-upgrades for p4 pools, pin provisioner image to 5.15 for critical capacity, start a canary 6.4 test on non-GPU hosts only.
sara: Pinning reduces our available GPU capacity by ~12% during the pin window (we'll need to spin spare hosts in other regions), cost estimate +18% for this week if we keep fallback nodes.
jon: Quick deploy attempt: installing matching driver (535.x) + dkms autoinstall then update-initramfs fixed a subset previously. Playbook: ```sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535 && sudo dkms autoinstall && sudo update-initramfs -u -k 6.4.0-rc```
chris: Tried that on a repro node — dkms autoinstall errors with unresolved symbols: 'unresolved symbol: nv_kthread_create', rebuild fails in post-install. So driver 535 prebuilt binary is not compatible with our custom kernel config.
nisha: Options: 1) pin kernels for GPU pools until driver vendor releases matching binaries, 2) build driver from source against kernel headers (slow, risky), 3) drain GPUs and fall back to CPU instances for low-priority workloads.
leo: I'm going to apply option 1 for the next 24h for p4-highprio and p4-prod pools. Starting hold on kernel-auto-update in the provisioner.
sara: If we fall back to CPU for batch customers, we need to notify CSM — cost + perf implications. I'll draft a short bulletin.
chris: I'll start a bisect on the driver ABI/patches and collect dkms logs + modinfo output. Uploading logs to s3: s3://redwood-debug/infra/kernel-6.4/dkms-1847654321.log
jon: Also check initramfs sequence — some nodes had udev ordering which removed headers before dkms runs. If that's the case, we can reorder the systemd unit to run dkms earlier.
eng-sre-bot: note: monitoring alert group 'gpu-module-fail' escalated to pagers at 12:12 UTC.
nisha: Good call. @chris can you paste the exact dkms error snippet here when available? I'll tag platform for a temporary hotfix script to run on repro nodes.
chris: posting truncated log: ```DKMS: build: make -j4 KERNELRELEASE=6.4.0-rc... gcc: error: unrecognized command line option '-mno-clobber'? make[1]: *** [Makefile:123: modules] Error 2```
sara: Thanks. Prioritize customer-facing mitigation so no SLA breach. Keep updates in this thread. :thumbsup:
leo: I'll coordinate with cloud partner about their kernel packaging and get a kernel-specialist on the call. Starting a brief freeze and canary plan.
nisha: Adding a task to infra board to track (kernel headers, driver rebuild, canary results, customer impact). Tagging @chris for follow-up.
chris: Will upload full dkms tarball in 30m and link in #incidents.
sara: Appreciate it — please ping me once we have the canary result or if we need an emergency rollback across regions.
